name: East Face

pitch_detail.notes: Start up the lower face; loose rock, moderate climbing with route-finding required.
Continues up the lower two-thirds of the face on looser but manageable rock.
Lower-face climbing continues; route-finding is key through this section.
Last of the lower, looser pitches before rock quality improves higher up.
Crux pitch — fingers-to-hand crack with excellent exposure below; the technical highlight of the route.
Opens with a burly roof/flake pull rated 5.8, then one of the best 5.8 hand cracks in the Washington Pass area.

rappel_detail.notes: First of about three single-rope rappels back to the approach talus; inspect existing fixed slings before weighting.
rappel_detail.anchor: slung horn/block, ~100ft (30m) west of the true summit past a short catwalk

rappel_detail.notes: Final rappel regaining the approach talus at the base.

rappels: About three single-rope (60m) rappels from slung anchors roughly 100 ft west of the true summit, down the descent gully back toward the base of the face
descent_text: From the top, one option is to traverse a short catwalk and build rappel anchors roughly 100 feet west of the true summit; another option is to rappel north until you can cross the gully separating Minuteman from Liberty Bell, then downclimb to a bush anchor for a final rappel. Either way, about three rappels on a single 60m rope typically regain the approach talus. Existing fixed slings around horns/blocks should be inspected (and backed up if in doubt) before weighting, since they're exposed to UV and rockfall.
approach: From Seattle, drive I-5 north to Burlington/Sedro-Woolley, then east on SR-20 through Marblemount and over Rainy Pass to Washington Pass; from Winthrop/Mazama it's a quick 20-30 minute drive west on SR-20 instead. Park beside the small pond on SR-20 a few hundred yards east of Washington Pass (about 5,400 ft). Walk around the pond's left side and take the climbers' path into the forest, heading roughly south-southwest; it comes out onto talus beneath the east walls of Liberty Bell and Minuteman near 6,000 ft. Work up the talus to Minuteman's lower left corner, around 6,600 ft. Plan on about an hour and roughly 1,200 ft of climbing from the car.
overview: A 6-pitch, Grade III 5.10- moderate alpine rock route up the East Face of the smallest tower in the Liberty Bell Group, climbing progressively better rock to a stellar hand-crack finish near the summit.
beta: The route ascends Minuteman's East Face, working up and slightly right through three to four pitches of looser, route-finding-dependent rock before the climbing dramatically improves in the final third: a 5.10 fingers-to-hand crux pitch with excellent exposure, followed by a burly 5.8 roof/flake move into one of the best 5.8 hand cracks at Washington Pass. accounts describe it variously as 5-6 or 6-7 pitches depending on how sections are linked; 6 pitches and 600 feet is the most commonly cited length.
gear: single 60m rope (the rappel descent works on one rope)
fa: Scott Davis and Bill Lingley, July 30, 1967
